# Scenix v1.9.0 — XR, Audio, And Physics Bridges

Scenix `1.9.0` adds three optional, `no_std`-capable CPU crates that bring
simulation-adjacent systems onto the scenix vocabulary without an engine,
OpenXR runtime, or audio SDK — `scenix-xr` (session planning, controller
bays, hand frames, anchors, planes, hit testing, light estimation), 
`scenix-audio` (spatial mixing, Doppler, analysis, streamed buffer health),
and `scenix-physics` (a deterministic penalty-based rigid-body solver with
sensors, queries, sleeping, and a jump-capable character controller) — plus
CPU-bridge scene nodes, camera stereo math, a WebXR fallback plan,
debug helpers, and facade integration. The renderer pipeline itself is
untouched: everything springs off the same deterministic CPU rules whether
the host is a game loop, a wasm demo, or an XR runtime host.

## Highlights

- `scenix-xr` is a standalone CPU crate (`std`/`serde`): `XrSessionPlan`
  validates mode/reference-space/feature combinations with
  `XrSessionPlanError` diagnostics and walks an explicit
  Idle→Requesting→Starting→Active→Paused/Ending→Ended lifecycle
  (`XrSessionState::can_transition`); `XrControllerBay` tracks both hands
  from pointer/grip poses with velocity-based kinematic prediction;
  `XrHandFrame` models the 26-slot hand profile (`JOINT_WRIST`,
  `JOINT_THUMB_TIP`, `JOINT_INDEX_TIP`) with tracked-joint accounting and
  thumb-index pinch distance; anchors (`XrAnchorStore` with age-based
  pruning), planes (`XrPlaneStore`), hit testing (`XrHitTestProbe` against
  floor/wall/window surfaces), and backward-compatible ambient-vs-light
  estimation plan the field systems; `XrFramePlan` carries per-frame stats,
  the swapchain `XrViewport` (tensor-scaled with the `XR_MAX_VIEWPORT_SCALE`
  clamp), and builds the stereo rig directly.
- `scenix-audio` is a standalone CPU crate: `AudioListener::axes` builds the
  orthonormal listeners; `compute_spatial_decision` folds pan weights,
  four attenuation models (`None`/`Linear`/`Inverse`/`InverseSquare` with
  gain-clamped far curves), WebAudio-convention cones, and
  `DopplerModel::shift` (speed-of-sound ratios, factor `0..=1`, clamped to
  `0.25..=4`) into one `SpatialDecision`; `compute_spatial_gain` finishes
  the stereo route. `AudioStreamPlan` tracks chunk buffering health
  (`accept_chunk`/`promote_pending`/`consume_chunk` + underrun counting) and
  `AudioAnalyser` meters mono/stereo input into RMS/peak plus three energy
  bands with smoothing. Constants like `SPEED_OF_SOUND`, `STREAM_MAX_CHUNKS`,
  and `AUDIO_LISTENER_MAX_SOURCES` bound the field sizes.
- `scenix-physics` is a standalone CPU crate: `PhysicsWorld::earth` runs a
  penalty-based solver — O(n²) AABB broad phase with collider groups,
  analytic narrow phase (sphere/box/capsule/plane pairs), restitution plus
  Coulomb friction plus a Baumgarte positional push (`CONTACT_RESOLVE_PERCENT`
  0.2, `CONTACT_SLOP` 5 mm), real substeps (`MAX_SUBSTEPS` 4 at ≤
  `MAX_SUBSTEP_DT` 1/120 s), linear speed clamping, and frame-threshold
  sleeping with wake events — all deterministic against body ordering.
  `Collider` attaches with sensor/density controls for group-filtered
  triggers; `cast_ray`/`overlap_sphere` answer spatial questions;
  `CharacterState::move_and_slide` walks a kinematic capsule with slope
  limits, step offsets, jumps, and probe-based ground snapping;
  `PhysicsTransformSync` batches the per-frame write list for scene
  integration.
- `scenix-scene` adds `NodeKind::XrAnchor{anchor_id}`,
  `NodeKind::AudioSource{source_id, listener_id}`, and
  `NodeKind::PhysicsBody{body_id, collider_id}` riders on the scene schema;
  `scenix-core` adds the matching `XrSessionId`, `XrAnchorId`,
  `AudioSourceId`, `AudioListenerId`, `PhysicsWorldId`, `PhysicsBodyId`,
  and `ColliderId` newtypes.
- `scenix-camera` gains the stereo surface: `XrFov` four-angle eye frusta,
  `XrEyeProjection` (symmetric helper plus the raw WebXR layout) producing
  WebGPU-convention projection matrices, and `XrCameraRig` coupling a head
  transform with eye separation into left/right view and view-projection
  matrices.
- `scenix-wasm` gains an `xr` feature and the front-end fallback plan:
  `webxr_fallback_plan(granted)` splits granted runtimes from the desktop
  emulation, `emulated_headset_rig` builds the standing desk stereo rig, and
  `emulated_controller_pose` parks a fallback controller down-forward from
  the head — the demo never dead-ends when `navigator.xr` is missing.
- `scenix-helpers` adds the debug pass surface: `PoseAxesHelper` draws an
  oriented triad (plus a `-Z` forward stick) for controllers and head rigs,
  `HandSkeletonHelper` wires the 26-slot hand profile through
  `HAND_LINKS`, and (behind the new `physics` feature)
  `ColliderDebugHelper` wireframes sensors apart from solid colliders via
  `debug_wireframe`/`debug_wireframe_world`.
- The facade gains `xr`, `audio`, `physics`, and `bridges` features. The
  bridge re-exports are curated lists because their module namespaces
  (`xr`, `audio`, `physics`, `world`, `sync`) would otherwise shadow the
  scene/input glob re-exports; `scenix-math` gains `floor`/`ceil`/`round`
  shims so `no_std` substeps and viewport math round identically on every
  target.

## Small Example

```rust
use scenix::{
    AttenuationModel, AudioListener, AudioStreamPlan, AudioSource, CharacterInput,
    CharacterState, ColliderShape, DopplerModel, PhysicsBody, PhysicsWorld, PlaybackState, Quat,
    RigidBodyKind, StreamFormat, Transform, Vec3, XrControllerBay, XrFeatures, XrHand, XrPose,
    XrReferenceSpace, XrSessionPlan, XrSessionState, XrTrackingStatus,
};

// 1. XR: validate and present a room-scale VR plan.
let mut xr = XrSessionPlan::immersive_vr()
    .with_reference_space(XrReferenceSpace::Stage)
    .with_features(XrFeatures::room_scale_vr());
xr.validate()?;
for state in [
    XrSessionState::Requesting,
    XrSessionState::Starting,
    XrSessionState::Active,
] {
    xr.advance(state)?;
}

// Controller bays track pointer/grip poses; prediction extrapolates them.
let mut bay = XrControllerBay::new();
bay.update(
    XrHand::Right,
    XrPose::from_position(Vec3::new(0.25, 1.0, -0.6)),
    XrTrackingStatus::Tracked,
);

// 2. Audio: face a listener down-range and let the spatial mix decide.
let listener = AudioListener::axes(Vec3::new(0.0, 1.5, 2.0), Vec3::NEG_Z, Vec3::Y);
let mut source = AudioSource::new(1, PlaybackState::Playing);
source.position = Vec3::new(-1.0, 1.0, -1.0);
let decision = scenix::compute_spatial_decision(
    &listener,
    &source,
    AttenuationModel::Inverse,
    1.0,
    &DopplerModel::default(),
);
assert!(decision.audible);

// 3. Physics: walk a capsule across a floor.
let mut world = PhysicsWorld::earth();
world.add_solid(
    PhysicsBody::new(Transform::IDENTITY).with_kind(RigidBodyKind::Static),
    ColliderShape::boxy(20.0, 0.5, 20.0),
);
let player = world.add_body(
    PhysicsBody::new(Transform::new(Vec3::new(0.0, 1.4, 0.0), Quat::IDENTITY, Vec3::ONE))
        .with_kind(RigidBodyKind::KinematicPosition),
);
world.attach_collider(player, ColliderShape::capsule(0.35, 0.55));
let mut controller = CharacterState::new(player, 0.35, 0.55);
controller.move_and_slide(&mut world, &CharacterInput::move_towards(Vec3::X, 3.0, 1.0 / 60.0));

// 4. Streamed audio health stays deterministic for music-reactive scenes.
let mut plan = AudioStreamPlan::new(4, StreamFormat::PcmF32, 48_000, 2);
plan.accept_chunk();
assert!(plan.promote_pending());
```

Feature gates: `xr`, `audio` and `physics` are independent facade features;
`bridges` enables all three at once; `scenix-wasm`'s `xr` feature carries
the browser fallback; `scenix-helpers`' `physics` feature carries the
collider wireframe helper. The renderer WGSL is untouched in this release.
